Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 1:

(p-5) Surat Yunus (peace be upon him), one hundred and nine verses, Meccan.

The same applies to what follows it up to Surat al-Nur.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Alif. Lam. Ra.﴾ Hamzah, ʿAli and Abu ʿAmr pronounce this and similar letters with imalah (inclination of the vowel). It is an enumeration of the letters, in the manner of a challenge. ﴿These are the verses of the Book﴾: a reference to the verses that the surah contains. "Al-Kitab" (the Book) means the surah. ﴿The Wise﴾: possessing wisdom, since it comprises it; or, meaning perfected (muhkam), free from falsehood and fabrication.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 2:

The hamza in ﴿Has it been a wonder for the people?﴾ is for the denial of their astonishment and of their marveling at it. ﴿That We have revealed﴾: the ism (subject) of kāna, and ʿajaban is its khabar (predicate). The lām in lil-nās is connected to an omitted element which is a ṣifah (qualifier) of ʿajaban; when it was placed before it, it became a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative). ﴿To a man from among them: warn the people﴾, meaning "that warn," or it is mufassirah (explanatory), since revelation contains the sense of speech. ﴿And give good news to those who believe that they will have﴾, meaning "that they will have." The sense of the lām in lil-nās is that they made it for themselves a wonder at which they marvel. What they marveled at was that revelation should come to a human being, and that he should be a man from the lower ranks of their men rather than one of their great notables. They used to say: "The wonder is that God did not find a messenger to send to the people except an orphan of Abu Talib." And that he should mention to them resurrection, warn with the Fires, and give good news of the Gardens. Each of these matters is not a wonder, because the messengers sent to nations were only human beings like them. And sending an orphan or a poor man is also not a wonder (p-6), because God Most High chooses for prophethood only the one who has gathered its causes; wealth and worldly preeminence are not among its causes. And resurrection for recompense for good and evil is the supreme wisdom. So how could it be a wonder? Rather, what is wondrous and repugnant to minds is the nullification of recompense. ﴿A firm footing of truth with their Lord﴾: that is, a precedence, a favor, and a lofty station. Since striving and precedence are by the foot, a beautiful accomplishment and a precedence were called a "foot," just as a blessing was called a "hand" because it is given by the hand, and "reach" (bāʿ) because its owner extends it. So it is said: "So-and-so has a foot in goodness." Its being attributed to truth indicates an increase in favor, and that it is among the great precedences; or it means a station of truth, or the precedence of happiness. ﴿The disbelievers said: "Indeed, this is clearly a sorcerer."﴾ In the Book, (la-siḥrun) is read by Madani, Basri and Shami readers; and whoever reads (lasāḥirun), this is a reference to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and it is evidence of their incapacity and their acknowledgment of him, even if they were lying in calling him a sorcerer.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 3:

﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself over the Throne﴾

That is, He took possession (istawla). The Judge is far exalted above place, and the Worshipped One above limits. ﴿He arranges﴾ — He decides and ordains according to the requirements of wisdom — ﴿the affair﴾: that is, the affair of all creation, and the affair of the dominion (malakut) of the heavens, the earth and the Throne. When He mentioned what points to His greatness and sovereignty, namely the creation of the heavens and the earth and His establishment over the Throne, He followed them with this clause to add further indication of greatness, and to show that no matter of the affairs goes beyond His decree and determination. Likewise His saying ﴿There is no intercessor except after His permission﴾ is evidence of His might and majesty. ﴿That is﴾ the Great, described by what has been described — ﴿Allah, your Lord﴾, and He is the One deserving of worship — ﴿so worship Him﴾: affirm His oneness, and do not associate with Him any of His creation, whether a human or an angel, let alone an inanimate object that neither harms nor benefits. ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ That is, will you not then reflect, so that you infer from the existence of benefits and advantages the existence of a Beneficent Reformer? (p-7)

﴿To Him is your return, all of you﴾ is a *ḥāl* (a circumstantial clause describing the state of the subject). It means: you will not return in the final outcome except to Him, so prepare yourselves for meeting Him. *Al-marji‘* (the return) can mean either the act of returning or the place of returning.

﴿The promise of Allah﴾ is a *maṣdar* (verbal noun) emphasizing His saying ﴿To Him is your return﴾. ﴿Truly﴾ (*ḥaqqan*) is a *maṣdar* emphasizing His saying ﴿the promise of Allah﴾.

﴿Indeed, He originates creation, then repeats it﴾ is an *isti'nāf* (a resumed, independent sentence) whose meaning is the *ta‘līl* (giving the reason) for the necessity of the return to Him.

﴿That He may recompense those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: that is, the wisdom behind the beginning of creation and its repetition is that He recompenses the responsible persons (*mukallafīn*) for their deeds.

﴿With justice﴾ (*bil-qist*) means with fairness. It is connected to *liyajziya* (that He may recompense), meaning: that He may recompense them according to His justice and that He may pay them their rewards in full. Or it means: according to their own *qist*, that is, by what they did in justice and fairness, and that they did not wrong themselves when they believed, since *shirk* (association of partners with Allah) is wrongdoing.

﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is a great wrong﴾ [Luqman: 13]. This second reading is more fitting for the contrast with His saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieved, they will have a drink of boiling water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾. And there is also a theological (*kalāmī*) reason for it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 5:

﴿He it is who made the sun a radiance﴾. The yā' in ḍiyā' (ضياء) is converted from a wāw in ḍawʾ (ضوء), because of the kasra before it. Qunbul (قُنْبُل) changed it into a hamza, because that is more pleasing for the vowel (لِلْحَرَكَةِ أجْمَلُ). ﴿And the moon a light﴾. Ḍiyā' is stronger than nūr (نور), so He assigned ḍiyā' to the sun. ﴿And He determined it﴾, and determined the moon, i.e., He determined its course ﴿in stations﴾, or He determined it as having stations, like His saying ﴿And the moon, We have determined it in stations﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 39]. ﴿That you may know the number of years﴾, i.e., the number of years and months, and He suffices with "years" because they include the months. ﴿And the reckoning﴾, and the reckoning of the terms and the appointed times determined by years and months. ﴿God did not create that﴾ mentioned ﴿except﴾ being connected ﴿with the truth﴾, which is the far-reaching wisdom, and He did not create it in vain. "Yufaṣṣilu al-āyāt" (يُفَصِّلُ الآياتِ) is read by Makkī, Baṣrī and Ḥafṣ, and with the nūn by others ﴿for a people who know﴾, who then benefit by reflecting upon them.

Verily in the alternation of the night and the day [﴿إنَّ في اخْتِلافِ اللَيْلِ والنَهارِ﴾], (understood as) in the coming of each of them after the other, or: in the difference of their two colors (i.e., light and darkness), [﴿وَما خَلَقَ اللهُ في السَماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾] and whatever Allah has created in the heavens and the earth of creatures, [﴿لآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَّقُونَ﴾] are signs for a people who are mindful (of Allah). He singled them out for mention because they fear the Hereafter, and that fear leads them to reflection.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 7:

﴿Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us﴾ do not expect it at all, nor does it occur to their minds, due to their heedlessness of perceiving the realities; or they do not hope for the good of meeting Us as the fortunate hope for it; or they do not fear the evil of meeting Us, which is what one should fear. ﴿And they are content with the worldly life﴾ instead of the Hereafter, and they prefer the little, perishing thing over the abundant, enduring thing. ﴿And they are at rest in it﴾ and they settle in it with the settling of one who is never disturbed from it, so they build firmly and hope far. ﴿And those who are heedless of Our signs﴾ do not reflect upon them, and there is no pause upon it, because the predicate of inna (إنَّ) is:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 8:

﴿Those, their abode is the Fire﴾. Fa-ulā'ika (ُulā'ika, "those") is a mubtada' (subject of a nominal sentence). Ma'wāhum (their abode) is a second mubtada'. Al-nār (the Fire) is its khabar (predicate), and the whole sentence (al-jumla) is the khabar of ulā'ika. The bā' in ﴿for what they used to earn﴾ is related to an omitted element (maḥdhūf) which the context indicates, and it is jūzū ("be recompensed").

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, their Lord will guide them by their faith﴾. He makes them firm, because of their faith, in *istiqamah* (steadfastness) upon the upright path that leads to reward. For this reason He made ﴿Rivers flow beneath them﴾ an explanation and elaboration of it, since holding fast to the means of happiness is like arriving at it. Or, it means that He will guide them in the Hereafter by the light of their faith to the path of Paradise. And from this is the hadith: "When the believer comes out of his grave, his deed will be presented to him in a beautiful form, and he will say to him, 'I am your deed,' and it will become for him a light and a guide to Paradise. And when the disbeliever comes out of his grave, his deed will be presented to him in an evil form, and he will say to him, 'I am your deed,' and it will set off with him until it brings him into the Fire." This is evidence that bare faith (*al-iman al-mujarrad*) saves, since He said "by their faith" and did not add righteous deeds to it. ﴿In Gardens of Bliss﴾: it is related to ﴿flow﴾, or it is a circumstantial phrase (*hal*) of ﴿the rivers﴾. (p-٩)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 10:

﴿Their call therein is: "Glory be to You, O Allah"﴾. That is, their supplication (du'a'). Because "Allahumma" (O Allah) is a vocative addressed to Allah, and its meaning is "O Allah, we glorify You." That is, they call upon Allah with their saying "Glory be to You, O Allah," delighting in His remembrance, not as worship (ʿibadah). ﴿And their greeting therein is: "Peace"﴾. That is, some of them greet one another with peace; or it is the greeting of the angels to them, and the verbal noun (al-masdar) is put in genitive construction with its object (idafah to the object); or it is Allah's greeting to them. ﴿And the last of their call﴾, meaning the conclusion of their supplication, which is the glorification (tasbih), ﴿is: "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾

"An" (أنْ) here is the lightened form (mukhaffafah) of the heavy "inna" (أنَّ), and its original form is "annahu al-hamdu lillahi rabbi al-alamin," with the pronoun referring to the matter/situation (damir al-shan). It has been said: the beginning of their speech is glorification and its end is praise, so they begin by magnifying Allah and declaring Him free of imperfection, and they conclude with thanks and commendation of Him, and between the two they speak of whatever they wish.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on Surah 10, verse 11:

﴿And if God were to hasten for people the evil as they hasten for the good﴾. Its original form is: "And if God were to hasten for people the evil in the same manner that they seek to hasten the good for themselves," so the phrase "their seeking to hasten the good" (*isti'jaluhum bil-khayr*) is put in place of "His hastening the good for them" (*ta'jilahu lahumu al-khayr*), to indicate how swiftly He answers them. The intended people are the people of Mecca, and their words are ﴿Then rain down on us stones from the sky﴾. That is, "If We hastened for them the evil which they called for, just as We hasten the good for them and answer them with it."

﴿Their term would have been decreed for them﴾: they would have been made to die and destroyed. "*Laqudiya ilayhim ajalahum*" is read by Ibn 'Amir (*Shami*, the Syrian reading) with the verb in the active voice, its subject being God, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿So We leave those who do not expect meeting Us in their rebellion﴾: in their polytheism and their misguidance. ﴿Wandering blindly﴾: hesitating and vacillating.

The connection of this with what precedes it is that God's words "And if God were to hasten" imply the negation of hastening, as if it were said: "We do not hasten for them the evil, nor do We decree their term for them, so We leave them in their rebellion," that is, "We grant them respite and pour out blessings upon them despite their rebellion, as a means of establishing the proof against them."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 12:

﴿And when harm touches man﴾ it afflicts him; and what is meant is the disbeliever. ﴿He calls upon Us﴾, i.e., he calls upon God to remove it, ﴿lying on his side﴾, in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), as indicated by the coordination of the two circumstances, i.e., ﴿or sitting or standing﴾ upon it. That is: he calls upon Us lying down. The purpose of mentioning these states is that one who is harmed does not cease calling, does not slacken in supplication until the harm is removed from him. So he calls upon Us in all his states: whether lying down, unable to rise; or sitting, unable to stand; or standing, unable to walk. ﴿But when We remove from him his harm﴾, i.e., We take away what afflicts him, ﴿he passes on as if he had never called upon Us against a harm that touched him﴾, i.e., he goes on in his former way as before the touch of harm, forgetting the state of hardship; or he passes on from the station of supplication and humble entreaty, not returning to it, as if he had no past association with it. The original would be "as if he had not called upon Us," but it was lightened and the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-sha'n) was deleted. ﴿Thus﴾, like that adornment, ﴿it is made attractive to the wasteful﴾, i.e., to those who exceed the limit in disbelief; Satan adorns it for them through his whispering, ﴿what they used to do﴾, namely turning away from remembrance and following disbelief.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 13:

﴿And We certainly destroyed the generations before you﴾ — O people of Makkah — ﴿when they committed wrong﴾, that is, they associated partners (with Allah). The word "when" (lamma) is an adverbial clause (zarf) governed by "We destroyed" (ahlaknā). The waw in ﴿and their messengers had come to them﴾ is a waw of the circumstantial state (wāw al-hāl), meaning: they committed wrong by denying, while their messengers had already come to them ﴿with clear proofs﴾, that is, with miracles. ﴿And they would not have been [such as] to believe﴾ if they had remained and had not been destroyed, because Allah knew about them that they would persist in their disbelief. This clause is either coordinated (ʿatf) with "they committed wrong" or is a parenthetical insertion (iʿtiraḍ). The lām (in liyu'minū) is for emphasis of the negation (lām al-taʾkīd lil-nafy). The meaning is that the cause of their destruction was their denial of the messengers, and Allah's knowledge that there was no benefit in granting them respite after the proof had been established against them through the sending of the messengers. ﴿Thus﴾, like that recompense, namely destruction, ﴿We recompense the guilty people﴾. This is a warning to the people of Makkah concerning their criminality in denying the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 14:

﴿Then We made you successors (khalā'if) in the earth after them.﴾ The address is to those to whom Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent. That is: We made you successors in the earth after the generations which We destroyed. ﴿That We may see how you act.﴾ That is: that We may see whether you do good or evil, so that We may deal with you according to your deeds. The word "how" (kayfa) is in the accusative position governed by ta'malūna ("you do"), not by nanẓura ("We may see"), because the meaning of interrogation in it prevents its governing word from preceding it. The meaning is: you are in our sight, so look how you act: is it by taking heed from your past (al-i'tibar bi-mādīkum) or by being deceived by what is in you (al-ightirar bi-mā fīkum)?

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The world is sweet and green, and indeed Allah is making you successors in it, and He will look at how you act."

﴿وَإذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا بَيِّناتٍ﴾ *(wa-idhā tutlā ʿalayhim āyatunā bayyinātin)*: the clause is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial clause, a clause describing the state in which the action occurs). ﴿قالَ الَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ لِقاءَنا﴾ *(qāla alladhīna lā yarjūna liqāʾanā)*: "Those who do not expect to meet Us say." When it angered them that the Qur'an condemned the worship of idols and threatened the people of tyranny, ﴿ائْتِ بِقُرْآنٍ غَيْرِ هَذا﴾ *(ʾti bi-Qurʾānin ghayri hādhā)*: "Bring a Qur'an other than this," one that does not contain what angers us about these things, "we will follow you." ﴿أوْ بَدِّلْهُ﴾ *(aw baddilhu)*: "or change it," by putting a verse of mercy in place of a verse of punishment and removing the mention of the gods and the condemnation of their worship. So he was commanded to answer regarding the substitution, because it falls within the power of a human being, which is to place a verse of mercy in place of a verse of punishment and to remove the mention of the gods. This is stated in His words ﴿قُلْ ما يَكُونُ لِي﴾ *(qul mā yakūnu lī)*: "Say: It is not for me," meaning it is not permissible for me, ﴿أنْ أُبَدِّلَهُ مِن تِلْقاءِ نَفْسِي﴾ *(an ubaddilahu min tilqāʾi nafsī)*: "to change it of my own accord," meaning on my own initiative. ﴿إنْ أتَّبِعُ إلا ما يُوحى إلَيَّ﴾ *(in attabiʿu illā mā yūḥā ilayya)*: "I follow only what is revealed to me," meaning I follow only the revelation of God, without addition, subtraction or alteration, because what I have brought is from God and not from me, so that I could change it. ﴿إنِّي أخافُ إنْ عَصَيْتُ رَبِّي﴾ *(innī akhāfu in ʿaṣaytu rabbī)*: "Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord," by altering it on my own account, ﴿عَذابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ *(ʿadhāba yawmin ʿaẓīmin)*: "the punishment of a great day," that is, the Day of Resurrection.

As for bringing another Qur'an, a human being cannot do that, and their inability to do so has become evident to them. However, they did not acknowledge their inability and would say, "If we willed, we would say the like of this" (*law nashāʾu la-qulnā mithla hādhā*). It is not possible that by their saying ﴿ائْتِ بِقُرْآنٍ غَيْرِ هَذا أوْ بَدِّلْهُ﴾ they meant it as coming from revelation, given His words ﴿إنِّي أخافُ إنْ عَصَيْتُ رَبِّي عَذابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾. Their purpose in this proposal was deceit (*al-kayd*). As for the proposal of replacing one Qur'an with another, it implies that it is from you and that you are able to produce its like, so replace it with another. As for the proposal of alteration, it is to test the situation: if any alteration came from him, then either God would destroy him and they would be rid of him, or God would not destroy him and they would mock him, making the alteration a proof against him and a confirmation of his fabrication against God.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 16:

﴿Say: "If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you through me."﴾ He means that its recitation is only by the will of Allah and His manifestation of a wondrous matter that is outside the customary norms, namely that an unlettered man, who had not studied and had not seen the scholars, should come forth and recite to you a book of eloquence that surpasses every eloquent speech and rises above every prose and poetry, laden with the sciences of the foundations (usul) and the branches (furu') of the law, and with reports of the unseen which no one knows except Allah. ﴿Nor would He have made you know of it﴾ — nor would Allah have informed you of the Qur'an through my tongue. ﴿For I had lived among you a lifetime before it﴾ — before the revelation of the Qur'an; that is, I had dwelt among you for forty years, and you knew me not to be practicing anything of its kind, nor was I capable of it, nor was I described as possessing knowledge or eloquence, so that you could accuse me of fabricating it. ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾ — so that you would know that it is nothing but from Allah, not from one like me. This is a response to what they concealed beneath their saying, "﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this﴾ [Yunus: 15]," namely their attribution of fabrication to him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 17:

﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾ It may be that it means the fabrication of the polytheists against Allah, in that He has a partner and has a son; and it may be that it is a disclaimer from what they attributed to Him of fabrication. ﴿Or denies His signs﴾ — that is, the Qur'an. In it is an explanation that the one who lies against Allah and the one who denies His signs are equal in disbelief. ﴿Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.﴾

﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which can neither harm them﴾ if they abandon its worship, ﴿nor benefit them﴾ if they worship it. ﴿And they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah"﴾, meaning the idols, ﴿"with Allah"﴾ meaning in matters of this world and its livelihood, because they did not affirm the resurrection (al-ba'th). ﴿And they swore by Allah with the utmost of their oaths: "Allah will not raise up one who dies"﴾ [al-Nahl: 38], or on the Day of Resurrection, if there is any resurrection and rising again. ﴿Say: "Will you inform Allah of what He does not know"﴾? That is, will you tell Him that they are intercessors with Him? This is informing Him of something that is not known to Allah. And if it is not known to Him, and He knows all that is known, then it is nothing. His words ﴿"in the heavens or on the earth"﴾ are an emphasis on its negation, because whatever does not exist in them is non-existent. ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted above what they associate﴾: He has declared His essence free from having any partner. With the ta' (تُشْرِكُونَ, "you associate"), Hamza and Ali read it. The word "mā" (ما) is either a relative pronoun (mawṣūla) or a verbal-noun particle (maṣdariyya). That is: "from the partners you associate with Him," or "from your association."

(p-13)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 19:

﴿And mankind was not but one community﴾ [who were] ḥunafā' (upright in faith), agreeing upon one religion (milla), without disagreeing among themselves. This was in the time of Adam (peace be upon him), until Qabil (Cain) killed Habil (Abel), or it was after the Flood, when Allah left none of the disbelievers dwelling upon the earth (dayyār). ﴿Then they differed﴾, so they became separate religions (milal). ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, namely the postponement of judgment between them until the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the matter would have been decided between them immediately﴾ ﴿concerning that over which they differ﴾, that is, concerning what they differed about, and so that the truthful (muḥiqq) might be distinguished from the falsifier (mubṭil). The predestination of His word is for a wisdom, which is that this abode is one of obligation (taklīf), and that abode is the abode of reward and punishment.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 20:

﴿They say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾ That is: a sign from among the signs that they proposed. ﴿So say: "The unseen belongs only to Allah."﴾ That is: He alone is the one specially knowledgeable of the unseen, so He alone knows what prevents the sending down of the proposed signs. ﴿So wait,﴾ for the descent of what you have proposed. ﴿Indeed, I am with you among those who wait,﴾ for what Allah will do to you because of your obstinacy and your denial of the signs.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 21:

﴿When We let the people, the people of Makkah, taste mercy﴾ meaning fertility and abundance, ﴿after hardship had touched them﴾ meaning drought and hunger, ﴿behold, they devise schemes against Our signs﴾. That is, they scheme against Our signs by repelling them and denying them. It is narrated that God, exalted is He, sent drought upon the people of Makkah for seven years, until they nearly perished. Then He showed them mercy with rain. When He showed them mercy, they began to slander God's signs and to oppose the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and plot against him. Here ﴿idha﴾ (then, suddenly) in the first place is the conditional (al-shart), and the second ﴿idha﴾ is its answer (al-jawab), and it is the particle of suddenness (al-mufaja'ah). It is like His saying: ﴿And if an evil befalls them because of what their hands have sent before, behold, they despair﴾ [al-Rum: 36]. That is: if an evil befalls them, they despair. And when We let the people taste mercy, they scheme. ﴿Makr﴾ (scheming) is concealing a plot and keeping it hidden, from the expression ﴿al-jariyah al-mamkurah﴾ (a girl of firm, closed character). The meaning of ﴿massathum﴾ (touched them) is that it mixed with them until they perceived the evil effect of it upon them. He said ﴿Say: God is swifter in scheming﴾ and did not describe them as swift in scheming, because the particle of suddenness indicated that. It is as if He said: when We show them mercy after hardship, they hasten to the occurrence of scheming on their part, and they rush to it before they have washed their heads of the touch of hardship. ﴿Indeed Our messengers﴾, meaning the guardian angels (al-hafazah, the recording angels), ﴿record what you scheme﴾. This is an announcement that what you think is hidden is not hidden from God, and He will take vengeance upon you. And with the ya' (reading yaktubun): it is easy.

(p-14)

﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea﴾: He makes you able to cover distances on foot, by riding animals, and by ships sailing on the seas, or He creates travel in you. "Yunshirukum" (﴿يَنْشُرُكُمْ﴾, "He spreads you out") is the reading of al-Shami (the Syrian reader, Ibn 'Amir). ﴿Until, when you are in the ships﴾: that is, in the vessels, ﴿and they sail with them﴾: with those on board. The shift from the second person to the third person is a shift from direct address to narrative, for emphasis. ﴿With a favorable wind﴾: gentle in its blowing, neither violent nor weak. ﴿And they rejoice in it﴾: in that wind, because of its gentleness and steadiness. ﴿There comes upon them﴾: that is, upon the ship, or upon the favorable wind, meaning: it meets them. ﴿A violent wind﴾: possessing violence, that is, of intense blowing. ﴿And the waves come upon them﴾: the waves are what rises above the water, ﴿from every place﴾: from the sea, or from all the places of the waves. ﴿And they think that they are encompassed﴾: that they are destroyed. The encompassing of an enemy around a tribe is made a metaphor for destruction. ﴿They call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾: without associating anything with Him, because at that time they do not call upon anything besides Him. They say: ﴿If You deliver us from this﴾: from these terrors, or from this wind, ﴿we will surely be among the thankful﴾: for Your blessing, believing in You and holding firmly to Your obedience.

He did not make being in the ship the goal of the travel at sea. Rather, the meaning of the conditional clause that follows "until" along with what it contains is as if it were said: "He makes you travel until, when this event occurs, and such-and-such happens, namely the coming of the violent wind, the piling up of the waves, the thought of destruction, and the calling for deliverance." The answer of "idha" (when) is ﴿there comes upon them﴾, and "they called" (﴿دَعَوُا﴾) is a substitute (badal) for "they thought" (﴿ظَنُّوا﴾), because their calling is a necessary consequence of their thinking they will perish, so it is connected to it. (p-15)

﴿Then when He had delivered them, behold, they were committing outrage in the earth﴾ corrupting in it, ﴿without right﴾, falsely, i.e., being wrongdoers. ﴿O mankind, your outrage is only against yourselves﴾, i.e., your wrongdoing returns upon you, like His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self, and whoever does evil, it is against it﴾ [Fussilat: 46]. ﴿The enjoyment of the worldly life﴾: Hafs reads it, meaning, "you enjoy the enjoyment of the worldly life." And "upon yourselves" is the predicate (khabar) of "your outrage." Others read it with a raised ending, on the basis that it is the predicate of "your outrage," and "upon yourselves" is its complement (silah), like His saying: ﴿So he oppressed them﴾ [al-Qasas: 76]. Its meaning is: "Your outrage is only against your equals." Or it is a predicate, and "enjoyment" is a predicate after a predicate. Or "enjoyment" is the predicate of a hidden subject (mubtada'), i.e., "it is the enjoyment of the worldly life."

And in a hadith: "The quickest of good in reward is keeping the ties of kinship, and the quickest of evil in punishment is oppression and a false oath." It is also reported: "Two things Allah hastens in this world: oppression and disobedience to one's parents." And from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "If a mountain were to oppress another mountain, the oppressor would be crushed." And from Muhammad ibn Ka'b: "Three qualities, whoever has them, they will be upon him: oppression, breaking covenant, and deceit." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Your outrage is only against yourselves﴾, ﴿and the evil plotting encompasses none but its own people﴾ [Fatir: 43], ﴿So whoever breaks his oath, he breaks it only against himself﴾ [al-Fath: 10], ﴿Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do﴾, i.e., We will inform you of it and recompense you for it.

﴿Indeed, the likeness of the life of this world is as water which We sent down from the sky﴾, from the clouds, ﴿and there mingled with it﴾, with the water, ﴿the vegetation of the earth﴾. That is: it became intertwined because of it, until some of it mixed with other parts of it. ﴿Of what men eat﴾, meaning the grains, fruits and herbs, ﴿and cattle﴾, meaning the grass. ﴿Until, when the earth takes on its adornment﴾, its decoration with plants and the variety of their colours, ﴿and is beautified﴾, and adorns itself with it. The original form is "tazayyanat", and the ta' was assimilated into the za' (idgham, the merging of two identical consonants), which is eloquent speech. The earth is described as "taking its adornment" by way of comparison with a bride who takes on fine garments of every colour, clothing herself and adorning herself with other kinds of finery. ﴿And its people think﴾, the people of the earth, ﴿that they have power over it﴾, that they are able to benefit from it, to gather its produce and to harvest its yield. ﴿Then Our command comes upon it﴾, Our punishment, which is the striking of its crop with some blight, after they had felt secure and were certain that it was safe, ﴿by night or by day, and We make it﴾, We make its crop, ﴿a harvested field﴾, resembling what is reaped from crops in its cutting down and uprooting, ﴿as if it had not flourished﴾, as if its crop had not grown lush, that is: it did not remain. The omission of the noun (in this case, "crop") in these places is necessary for the meaning to be sound. ﴿Yesterday﴾, this is an expression for a recent time, as if it were said: "as if it had not flourished a moment ago." ﴿Thus do We detail the signs for a people who reflect﴾, so that they benefit from the coining of parables. This is a compound simile (tashbih murakkab, a likeness made of a whole picture): the condition of this world, in the swiftness of its passing and the vanishing of its delights after they have come, is likened to the condition of the plants of the earth in their drying up and their going away as chaff, after they had grown thick and dense and had adorned the earth with their greenness and their lush freshness. The wisdom of the comparison is to draw attention to the fact that the purity of life is its youth, and its turbidity is its old age, just as the clear part of water is at the top of the vessel. A poet said:

*Do you not see that life is a cup of pure wine:
its beginning is purity, and its end is turbidity?*

Its reality is the adorning of a lump of clay with the interests of this world and of religion, like the mingling of plants of various colours. So the good clay produces gardens of intimacy, the sweet basil of the spirit, the flower of asceticism, the vines of generosity, the grains of love, the orchards of truth and the anemones of the path. [Page 17] The bad clay produces the opposite of righteousness, the thistle of sin, the thorn of polytheism, the wormwood of stinginess, the firewood of ruin and the chaff of play. Then its return (to the earth) calls it, as its harvest comes due for the field, and life departs from it while it is deceived, just as the plant withers while turning yellow. Its body is then hidden in the grave, "as if it had not flourished yesterday", until the spring of resurrection returns, and the appointed time of the gathering and the examination. Likewise is the condition of this world: like water, its little benefits, and its great quantity destroys. There is no escape from leaving what exceeds one's need, just as one cannot avoid taking provisions. The one who takes wealth does not escape a slip, just as one who wades into water does not escape getting wet. Gathering it and holding it back is the destruction of its owner and his ruin. So what is below the minimum threshold (nisab, the amount at which zakat becomes obligatory) is like a shallow pool of water that one crosses without need for protection. The nisab is like a river standing between the one crossing and the crossing to the desert of safety, which cannot be traversed except by a bridge, and that is zakat. Its maintenance is the giving of gifts. When the bridge is broken, the waves of the arches (qanatir) drown him. On this, he (ﷺ) said, peace be upon him: "Zakat is the bridge of Islam." Similarly, wealth assists the base and not the noble, just as water gathers in the lowlands and not on the heights. Likewise, wealth is not gathered except through the toil of the miser, just as water is not gathered except by blocking the channel. Then it perishes and is destroyed, and does not remain, like water in the palm of the hand.

God calls to the Abode of Peace (Dar al-Salam). This is Paradise. He attributes it to His own name to glorify it, or because it is the abode of peace and safety, since its people are safe from every hated thing. It was also said that it is so named because of the frequent exchange of greetings of peace among its people and the angels' greeting of peace upon them, as in ﴿except the saying: "Peace, peace"﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 26]. ﴿And He guides whom He wills﴾, meaning He grants success to whom He wills, ﴿to a straight path﴾, meaning to Islam, or to the path of the Sunnah (the prophetic way and practice). So the calling is general, upon the tongue of the Messenger of God through indication, while the guidance is specific, from the gentle kindness of the One who sends, through success and special care. The meaning is: He calls all the servants to the Abode of Peace, and none enters it except those who are guided.

(p-18) ﴿For those who did good﴾: those who believed in Allah and His messengers. ﴿The best [reward]﴾: the best reward, which is Paradise. ﴿And more﴾: the sight of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic. This is reported from Abu Bakr, Hudhayfah, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with them all. In some exegetical works it is stated: "The exegetes agreed that the 'more' is looking upon Allah, exalted is He."

From Suhayb, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'Do you want anything more that I should give you?' They say: 'Did You not whiten our faces? Did You not admit us into Paradise and save us from the Fire?' Then He lifts the veil, and they look upon Allah, Exalted is He. Nothing has been given to them that is dearer to them than looking at their Lord." Then he recited: ﴿For those who did good is the best [reward] and more﴾.

It is strange that the author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari) mentioned this hadith without this wording and said: "It is a rejected hadith," although it is marfu' (traced to the Prophet). Al-Baghawi, the author of al-Masabih, included it in al-Sihah (in his collection of sound hadiths).

It is also said that the "more" is the love placed in the hearts of the servants. It is said that the "more" is forgiveness from Allah and His pleasure.

﴿And no dust shall cover their faces﴾: no gloom shall cover their faces. ﴿Nor humiliation﴾: nor any trace of disgrace. The meaning is that there shall not befall them what befalls the people of the Fire.

﴿Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein forever.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 27:

﴿And those who earned evil deeds﴾ is a conjunction (ʿaṭf) on "for those who did good" (lil-ladhīna aḥsanū), meaning: and for those who earned ﴿evil deeds﴾, i.e., the varieties of polytheism (shirk), ﴿the recompense of an evil deed is its like﴾. The bāʾ (in bi-mithlihā) is superfluous (zāʾida), as in His saying: ﴿And the recompense of an evil deed is an evil deed like it﴾ [al-Shura: 40]. Or the estimate is: the recompense of an evil deed is one measured by its like (muqaddaratun bi-mithlihā). ﴿And humiliation will cover them﴾: abasement and disgrace. ﴿They will have none from Allah﴾: from His punishment. ﴿Any protector﴾: meaning, no one will shield them from His wrath and punishment. ﴿As though their faces had been covered with pieces of the dark night﴾: meaning, a covering of the blackness of the night has been placed over them, i.e., they have black faces. "Qiṭaʿan" is the plural of qiṭʿa, and it is the second object (mafʿūl thānin) of ughshiyat. "Qiṭʿan" is read by Makkī and ʿAlī, from His saying: "bi-qiṭʿin min al-layl" [Hud: 81]. On this reading, muẓlliman is an adjective (ṣifa) of qiṭʿ; on the first reading it is a circumstantial state (ḥāl) of "al-layl", and its governing element (ʿāmil) is ughshiyat, because "min al-layl" is an adjective of qiṭʿan, so its governing of the qualified noun is like its governing of the adjective; or the meaning of the verb is "min al-layl". ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; therein they will abide forever﴾.

﴿And the day We gather them all﴾, i.e., the disbelievers and others, ﴿all together﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative, describing the state of the subject at the time of the action). ﴿Then We will say to those who associated [others with Allah]﴾, i.e., "Remain in your place and do not stir until you see what will be done to you." ﴿You﴾ is an emphatic pronoun for the pronoun in ﴿your place﴾ (مَكانَكم), since it stands in place of the phrase "remain" (الزَمُوا). ﴿And your partners﴾ is coordinated (ʿaṭf) with it. ﴿And We will separate them﴾, i.e., We will divide them and sever their bonds with one another, and the ties that existed between them in the world. ﴿And their partners will say﴾, meaning those they worshipped besides Allah, whether rational beings or idols that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will cause to speak: ﴿You did not worship us﴾. Rather, you were worshipping the devils, since they commanded you to set up rivals to Allah, and you obeyed them. This is His saying: ﴿And the day He gathers them all, then He will say to the angels: "Did these people worship you?"﴾ [Saba': 40], up to His saying ﴿Rather, they used to worship the jinn﴾ [Saba': 41].

Translation:

﴿Sufficient is God as a witness between us and you﴾, meaning: God is sufficient as a witness. The word "shahidan" (as a witness) is a tamyiz (specification of the noun, an accusative clarifying the sense of the preceding word). ﴿Indeed, we were unaware of your worship﴾. "In" (إنْ, indeed) is a lightened form of the heavy "inna," and the lam is a distinguishing particle (lam al-fariqa) separating it from the negative "in" (إنْ, not).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 30:

﴿Hunalika﴾ (there), in that place or in that time, on the basis of using the noun of place for time. ﴿Tablu kullu nafsin﴾ (every soul will test and experience) ﴿ma aslafat﴾ (what it sent forth) of deeds, so it will know how it is: is it ugly or good, beneficial or harmful, accepted or rejected? Al-Zajjaj said: every soul will know what it has sent forth. ﴿Tatlu﴾ (with the verb read as "taclu" with a ta and without a long vowel, meaning "follows") is the reading of Hamza and Ali, that is, it follows what it sent forth, because its deed is what guides it to the path of Paradise or Hell. Or it reads in its record what it sent forth of good or evil. This is also related from al-Akhfash. ﴿Wa ruddu ila Allahi mawlahumu al-haqq﴾ (and they are returned to God, their true Lord), their Lord who is truthful in His lordship, because they used to take as lords what in truth has no lordship; or the One who takes account of them and their reward, the Just who does not wrong anyone. ﴿Wa dalla anhum ma kanu yaftarun﴾ (and what they used to fabricate will be lost to them), what they used to claim, that they were partners of God, will vanish from them, or what they used to invent of lies and the intercession of the gods will be nullified for them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 31:

﴿Say, "Who provides for you from the heaven"﴾ by the rain, ﴿and the earth﴾ by the plants, ﴿or who controls hearing and sight?﴾ Who is able to create them both and shape them to the measure upon which they were shaped from a wondrous drop; or who protects them from calamities despite their abundance over long periods, while they are delicate, so that the slightest thing harms them. ﴿And who brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living?﴾ That is, the animal from the egg, the chick from the egg, the plant from the seed, the believer and the knowing one from the drop and the egg and the grain, and the disbeliever and the ignorant one from them, and the reverse. ﴿And who arranges the affair?﴾ Who takes charge of the management of the affair of the whole world. He has brought it in generality after specificity. ﴿They will say, "Allah."﴾ They will answer you when you ask them: the One capable of these things is Allah. ﴿So say, "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ [Will you not fear] associating partners with Him in worship, since you have acknowledged His lordship (al-rububiyyah).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 32:

﴿So that is Allah﴾, i.e., the one whose power is such, he is Allah, ﴿your Lord, the Truth﴾, whose lordship is established (al-thabit) with a firmness that admits no doubt for the one who examines (haqqaqa al-nazar) thoroughly. ﴿So what is there after the truth but error?﴾, i.e., there is no intermediate position between truth and error; whoever transgresses the truth falls into error. ﴿Then how are you turned away?﴾ from the truth to error, and from monotheism (tawhid) to polytheism (shirk).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 33:

﴿Kadhalika﴾ (Thus, just as this) truth, ﴿the word of your Lord has come true﴾. "Kalimat" (word) is the reading of Ibn 'Amir (al-Shami) and Madani (Nafi' of Madina), meaning: just as it is established and confirmed that after the truth there is only error, or just as it is established that they are turned away from the truth, so the word of your Lord has come true ﴿against those who have defied (fasaqu)﴾, that is, they persisted in their disbelief and went to its furthest limit. ﴿That they do not believe﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "the word": that is, it is decreed against them that faith is negated; or, the word of God has been decreed against them, that their faith will not occur (p-21); or by "the word" is meant the promise of punishment. And "that they do not believe" is a causal clause (ta'lil), meaning: because they do not believe.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 34:

﴿Say: "Is there any of your partners who originates creation and then repeats it?"﴾ He mentioned "then repeats it" though they did not acknowledge the repetition (i'adah), because its proof is so manifest that it was treated as an established matter. Or, among them there are those who acknowledge the repetition, or it may refer to the repetition of things other than humans, such as the repetition of night and day and the repetition of the sending down (of rain) and of plants. ﴿Say: "Allah originates creation and then repeats it."﴾ He commanded His Prophet to answer on their behalf, meaning: their obstinacy does not allow them to utter the word of truth, so speak on their behalf. ﴿Then how are you turned away?﴾ meaning: how are you diverted from the straight path?

Say: "Is there any of your partners who guides to the truth?" (i.e., who guides to it). Say: "God guides to the truth. Is the one who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or the one who cannot guide [himself] unless he is guided?"

It is said: one says *hadāhu lil-ḥaqq* and *hadāhu ilā al-ḥaqq* (he guided him to the truth), so [the Qur'an] combines the two idioms. It is also said that *hadā* by itself can mean *ihtadā* (to be guided), just as *sharā* means *ishtarā* (to buy). From this is the *qirā'a* (canonical recitation) of Ḥamzah and ʿAlī, *amman lā yahdī*, meaning *yahtadī* (is guided). *Lā yahaddī* with a fatḥa (short vowel "a") on the yā' and the hā' and a shadda (gemination mark) on the dāl is the reading of Makkī, Shāmī and Warsh. With *ishmām* (a slight rounding of the vowel, here toward a fatḥa) on the hā', it is the reading of Abū ʿAmr. With a kasra (short vowel "i") on the hā' and a fatḥa on the yā', it is the reading of ʿĀṣim, other than Yaḥyā. The original form is *yahtadī*, and this is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh. The tā' was assimilated into the dāl, the hā' was given a fatḥa with the vowel of the tā', and it was given a kasra because two sākin letters (letters with no vowel) met. With a kasra on the yā' and the hā' and a shadda on the dāl, it is the reading of Yaḥyā, to follow what comes after it. With a sukūn (absence of vowel) on the hā' and a shadda on the dāl, it is the reading of Madanī, other than Warsh.

The meaning is that God alone is the one who guides to the truth, through the intellects He placed in those who are responsible (*mukallafīn*), and the capacity He gave them to reflect on the proofs He set up for them, and through the success He granted them, the inspiration He placed in them, and His making them aware of the laws by sending the messengers. So: is there any of your partners, whom you have made rivals (*andād*) of God, who guides to the truth in the manner of God's guidance?

Then He said: "Is the one who guides to the truth more worthy of being followed, or the one who does not guide," that is, who does not guide himself, or who is not guided by others unless God guides him. It was also said that its meaning is: "or the one who, of the idols, cannot find his way to a place so as to move to it, unless he is moved (*yuhdā ilā an yunqala*)," or who does not find guidance, and guidance cannot be attributed to him unless God changes his state, making him living and speaking, so that He guides him.

So what is the matter with you? How do you judge? That is, judging falsely, in that you claim that they are rivals of God.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 36:

﴿And most of them follow nothing but conjecture﴾ in their saying to the idols that they are gods and that they are intercessors with God. The intended meaning of "most" (al-akthar) is all of them. ﴿Except conjecture﴾ without any proof, and this is their following their forefathers, supposing that they are correct. ﴿Surely conjecture avails nothing against the truth﴾, which is knowledge, ﴿at all﴾ (shay'an), which is in the place of the verbal noun, meaning: it gives no sufficiency (ighna'an). ﴿Surely God is Knowing of what they do﴾ of following conjecture and abandoning the truth.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 37:

﴿And this Qur'an could not have been fabricated apart from Allah﴾. That is, it could not be a fabrication apart from Allah. The meaning is: it was not correct or fitting that anything like it, in the sublimity of its matter and its inimitability, should be a fabrication. ﴿But﴾ it was ﴿a confirmation of what lies between its hands﴾, meaning what preceded it of the revealed Books, ﴿and a detailed explanation of the Book﴾, meaning a clarification of what has been prescribed and enjoined of rulings and laws, from His saying "the Book of Allah prescribed for you" (kitab Allah 'alaykum). ﴿There is no doubt in it, from the Lord of the worlds﴾ falls within the scope of the istidrak (the grammatical device of correction or qualification), as if he had said: "But it was a confirmation and a detailed explanation, free from doubt, coming from the Lord of the worlds." It is also permissible that the meaning be: "But it was a confirmation from the Lord of the worlds and a detailed explanation from Him, there is no doubt in that." In that case ﴿from the Lord of the worlds﴾ is connected to "confirmation" and "detailed explanation," and ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾ is a parenthetical insertion (i'tiradan), as when you say: "Zayd - there is no doubt about it - is generous."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 38:

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ Rather, do they say, "He has fabricated it"? Say: "If the matter is as you claim, ﴿then bring﴾ yourselves, in the manner of fabrication, ﴿a surah like it﴾, i.e., one resembling it in eloquence and excellence of composition, for you are like me in the Arabic language. ﴿And call upon whomever you can, apart from God﴾, i.e., call upon, apart from God, whomever you can of His creation to help you in producing the like of it, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ that he has invented it."

﴿Rather, they denied what they had not encompassed in knowledge, and its interpretation had not yet come to them﴾. *Bal sara'u ila al-takdhib bil-Qur'an fi badihat al-sama'* (Rather, they hastened to deny the Qur'an at the first hearing), *qabla an yafqahuhu wa-ya'lamu kunha amrihi* (before they understood it and knew the reality of its matter), *wa-qabla an yatadabbaruhu wa-yaqifu 'ala ta'wilihi wa-ma'anihi* (and before they reflected upon it and came to know its interpretation (ta'wil) and its meanings). This was due to *farṭ nufurihim 'amma yukhalifu dinahum* (their extreme aversion to whatever opposes their religion) *wa-shiradihim 'an mufaraqat dini aba'ihim* (and their fleeing from abandoning the religion of their fathers).

The sense of expectation (tawaqquʿ) in *"wa-lamma ya'tihim ta'wiluhu"* is that they denied it immediately at first hearing, before reflection and before knowing its ta'wil, by imitating their fathers (taqlid). Then they denied it after reflection, out of rebellion and obstinacy. So He censured them for their haste in denying it before knowing it. He used the word *lamma* (not yet) to indicate that they afterwards came to know its exalted status and its inimitability (i'jaz), when He repeatedly challenged them (tahaddi) and they tested their powers in opposition (mu'aradah) and recognized their inability to produce its like. Then they denied it out of insolence and envy.

﴿Thus﴾, in the same manner of denial, *﴿kadhdhaba alladhina min qablihim﴾* (those before them denied), meaning the disbelievers of the earlier nations denied their messengers before looking into their miracles and before reflecting upon them, out of obstinacy and imitation of their fathers.

It is also permissible that the meaning of *"wa-lamma ya'tihim ta'wiluhu"* is: "the ta'wil of what it contains of information about the unseen has not yet come to them," that is, its outcome, *hatta yatabayyana lahum a-huwa kadhibun am sidqun?* (so that it becomes clear to them whether it is a lie or the truth). This means that it is a book inimitable from two aspects: from the aspect of the inimitability of its composition (nazm), and from the aspect of the information about the unseen that it contains. So they hastened to deny it before looking into its composition and its reaching the limit of inimitability, and before testing its information about unseen matters and its truthfulness or falsehood.

﴿So look how was the end of the wrongdoers﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 40:

﴿And among them are those who believe in it﴾, in the Prophet or in the Qur'an, meaning: he affirms it inwardly and knows that it is true, but he obstinately denies it. ﴿And among them are those who do not believe in it﴾, who do not affirm it and are in doubt about it. Or the verb is in the future sense, meaning: among them are those who will believe in it, and among them are those who will persist (in disbelief). ﴿And your Lord knows best the corrupters﴾, meaning: the obstinate ones or the persistent ones.

﴿And if they deny you﴾, [meaning] even if they persist in denying you and you have despaired of their responding to you. ﴿Then say: "For me is my work﴾, meaning the recompense for my work, ﴿and for you is your work﴾, meaning the recompense for your deeds, ﴿you are free from what I do, and I am free from what you do﴾. [p. 24] So each one will be held accountable for his own deeds.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 42:

﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾ — And among them are people who listen to you when you recite the Qur'an and make known the sharia (sharā'i') — but they do not comprehend (lā ya'ūn) nor accept, so they are like the deaf. ﴿Can you make the deaf hear, even though they do not understand?﴾ Do you expect that you can cause the deaf to hear, when their deafness is compounded by the absence of their intellects? For a deaf person who is intelligent may perceive and infer, when the sound of a noise reaches his ear-canal (ṣimākh); but when the removal of intellect and hearing come together, then the matter is complete.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 43:

﴿And among them are those who look at you.﴾ And among them are people who look at you and witness the proofs of truthfulness and the signs of prophethood, but they do not believe. ﴿Would you then guide the blind, even though they cannot see?﴾ Do you suppose that you can guide the blind, even if the loss of sight is joined by the loss of insight? For the blind man who has insight in his heart may well perceive by conjecture (yahdis), whereas blindness combined with foolishness is the utmost affliction. It means that they are in despair of accepting and believing, like the deaf and the blind who have neither intellects nor insights.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 44:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people in anything, but it is the people who wrong themselves.﴾ "Wa-lakin an-nasu" (with the nasb/rafʿ reading as recited): Hamzah and ʿAli [read it so]. That is: He has not wronged them by depriving them of the instrument of reasoning (ālat al-istidlāl), but they wronged themselves by abandoning reasoning (tark al-istidlāl), in that they worshipped inanimate objects (jamād) while they were living beings.

[p. 25] And Ḥafṣ reads *yaḥshuruhum* with the *yā'* (وَبِالْيَاءِ), i.e., "He will gather them."

﴿And on the Day He will gather them, [it will be] as if they had not remained but an hour of the day﴾. They consider the length of their stay short, whether in the world or in their graves, because of the terror of what they see. ﴿They will recognize one another﴾: each one knows the other, as if they had been separated only briefly. This happens when they come out of the graves. Then recognition among them ends because of the severity of the matter upon them.

*Ka'anna lam yalbathū* (كَأنْ لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا, "as if they had not remained") is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial clause, a clause describing the state of the subject) referring back to *hum* ("them"). The meaning is: We will gather them, likening them to people who remained only an hour. *Ka'anna* (كَأنْ) is a *mukhaffafa* (lightened form of the heavy particle *inna*), and its noun is omitted, the full form being *ka'annahum*. *Yata'ārafūna baynahum* (يَتَعارَفُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ, "they recognize one another") is either a *ḥāl* following another *ḥāl*, or a *mustaʾnaf* (a new, independent sentence), on the understanding "they recognize one another."

﴿Indeed, the losers are those who denied the meeting with Allah﴾. This is either on the assumption of a saying, meaning: they recognize one another, saying this; or it is a testimony from Allah concerning their loss. The meaning is that they lost in their trade and their dealing, having exchanged faith for disbelief. ﴿And they were not guided﴾ in the trade, knowing it. This is a *mustaʾnaf* (new sentence) carrying the sense of wonder, as if it were said: "How great their loss!"

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 46:

﴿And whether We show you some of what We threaten them with﴾ of the punishment ﴿or cause you to die﴾ before their punishment ﴿—to Us they will return﴾ is the response to "or cause you to die." The response to "whether We show you" is omitted, meaning: "Whether We show you some of what We threaten them with in this world, so be it, or We cause you to die before We show it to you, and We will show it to you in the Hereafter." ﴿Then Allah is Witness over what they do﴾. Witness has been mentioned, but what is meant is its requirement, which is punishment, as if it were said: "Then Allah is the One who punishes them for what they do." It has also been said that "thumma" (then) here carries the meaning of "wa" (and).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 47:

﴿And for every nation there is a messenger﴾ who is sent to them in order to awaken them to monotheism (tawhid) and to invite them to the religion of truth. ﴿So when their messenger comes﴾ with the clear proofs, and they deny him and do not follow him, ﴿judgment is passed between them﴾, between the Prophet and those who denied him, ﴿with justice﴾, that is, with fairness: the messenger is saved and those who denied are punished. Or, it means: for every nation of the nations there is a messenger on the Day of Resurrection, to whom they are attributed and by whom they are called. So when their messenger comes to the place of standing (al-mawqif) to bear witness against them concerning disbelief and belief, judgment is passed between them with justice. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾, meaning that no one will be punished for a sin other than his own.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 48:

And when [Allah] said, ﴿Whether We show you some of what We promise them﴾ [Yunus: 46], meaning: of the punishment, they hastened [to ask] for what they were promised of the punishment. Then [Allah] revealed: ﴿And they say, "When is this promise?"﴾, meaning: the promise of punishment, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ that the punishment is coming down. This is an address from them to the Prophet and the believers.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 49:

﴿Say﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿"I possess not for myself any harm"﴾ from illness or poverty, ﴿"nor any benefit"﴾ from health or wealth, ﴿"except what Allah wills"﴾. This is an exceptive clause of disconnection (istithna' munqati'), meaning: rather, whatever Allah wills of that comes to pass. So how could I possess for you harm or the bringing of punishment? ﴿"For every community there is a term. When their term comes, they cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they advance it"﴾. For every community there is a known time for punishment, written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh). When the time of their punishment comes, they cannot go ahead of it by an hour nor fall behind it. So do not be hasty.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 50:

﴿Say: Have you considered: if His punishment comes upon you﴾ which you are hastening (tasta'jiluna) ﴿by night (bayatan)﴾ — it is put in the accusative as an adverb of time, meaning "at a time of night," and bayat is the night — ﴿or by day﴾ while you are occupied with seeking livelihood and gain, ﴿what is it that the guilty seek to hasten of it?﴾ That is, of the punishment. The meaning is that punishment in its entirety is something disliked and necessarily produces aversion, so what is it that you are hastening for, when there is nothing in it that would call for hastening? The interrogative in "what" (madha) is connected to "have you considered" (ara'aytum), because the meaning is: "Tell me, what is it that the guilty seek to hasten of it?" The response of the conditional is omitted, and it is: "you will regret hastening it, or you will recognize the error in it." It was not said "what is it that you (plural) hasten of it," because the intention was to indicate the consequence of abandoning hastening, which is criminality. Or, "what is it that the guilty seek to hasten of it?" is the response of the conditional, like: "If I come to you, what will you feed me?" and then the sentence is connected to "have you considered." Or:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 51:

﴿Then, when it [the punishment] befalls you, [will you say], "Now you believe in it"?﴾ The response of the conditional (shart) is ﴿you believe in it﴾, and "What then do the criminals seek to hasten of it?" is a parenthetical interjection (i'tiraD). The meaning is: if His punishment comes upon you, you will believe in it after its occurrence, at a time when faith will not benefit you. The entry of the interrogative particle (harf al-istifham) upon "thumma" (then) is like its entry upon the waw and the fa' in "Then are the people of the towns secure...?" and "Or are the people of the towns secure...?" and "His saying: 'I will surely fill Hell...'" (the verse), [all of which are] according to the intention of a saying, meaning: it will be said to them, when they believe after the punishment has befallen them: "Now [do you believe in it]?" ﴿And you used to seek to hasten it﴾, that is, the punishment, [by way of] denial and mockery. "Ālān" (now), with the deletion of the hamza that follows the lam and the transfer of its vowel onto the lam, is [the reading of] Nafi'.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 52:

﴿Then it will be said to those who did wrong﴾ — a conjunction (ʿatf) upon the implied saying (qawl) mentioned before "now" — ﴿Taste the punishment of eternity﴾, i.e., of perpetuity (al-dawam) — ﴿Are you being recompensed except for what you used to earn?﴾ — that is, from polytheism (shirk) and denial (takdhib).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 53:

﴿And they ask you (wa-yastanbi'unnaka)﴾ meaning: they ask you for information (wa-yastakhbirunaka), so they say, ﴿"Is it true (aḥaqqun huwa)?"﴾ This is a question in the manner of denial and mockery. The pronoun (huwa) refers to the promised punishment. ﴿Say (qul)﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿"Yes, by my Lord (iy wa-rabbī)"﴾ meaning: yes, by Allah. ﴿"Indeed it is true (innahu la-ḥaqq)"﴾ meaning: the punishment is certainly coming, without doubt. ﴿"And you cannot escape (wa-mā antum bi-mu'jizīn)"﴾ meaning: you cannot escape the punishment, and it will certainly overtake you without doubt.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 54:

﴿And if every soul that had wronged had possession of whatever is on the earth, it would surely offer it as ransom﴾ — "had wronged" means it disbelieved and associated partners (with God). The phrase "that had wronged" is a qualifier of "soul," meaning: and if every wrongdoing soul had whatever is on the earth in this world today of its treasures and wealth, ﴿it would surely offer it as ransom﴾, i.e., it would make it a ransom for itself. It is said: "fada-hu fa-iftada" (he ransomed him, so he ransomed himself), and it is also said: "iftada-hu," with the same meaning as "fada-hu." ﴿And they will conceal the regret when they see the punishment﴾ — and they will display it, from their saying "asarra al-shay'" when he displayed it; or they will conceal it, being unable to speak because of the severity of the matter, so "asarra" is among the words with contrary meanings (addad). ﴿And it will be judged between them with justice﴾ — between the wrongdoers and the wronged; the mention of wrongdoing indicates this. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾.

Then He followed this announcement, that the entire dominion belongs to Him, with His saying: ﴿Surely to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ So how could He accept ransom? And He is the One who rewards and punishes. As for what He promised of reward or punishment (p-28), it is true, by His saying: ﴿Surely the promise of Allah is true﴾ concerning reward or punishment, it is a truth that will come to pass. ﴿But most of them do not know.﴾

﴿He gives life and causes death﴾: He is the One able to give life and to cause death; none other than Him is able to do either. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾: the return is to His reckoning and His recompense, so one fears Him and hopes in Him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 57:

﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord﴾ That is: there has certainly come to you a Book comprising these benefits, an admonition and a reminder concerning Tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness). The mawizah (admonition) is that which calls to everything desired and restrains from everything feared. Thus, whatever in the Qur'an of commands (al-awamir) and prohibitions (al-nawahi) calls to everything desired and restrains from everything feared, since a command necessitates the goodness of the one commanded, so it is desired; and it necessitates the prohibition of its opposite, which is ugly. The same applies to prohibition. ﴿And a healing for what is in the breasts﴾ That is, for what is in your breasts of corrupt beliefs. ﴿And guidance﴾ from misguidance, ﴿and a mercy for the believers﴾ for whoever among you believes in it.

**"Say," O Muhammad, "By the bounty of Allah and His mercy, let them rejoice in that."** The original sense of the sentence is: "By the bounty of Allah and His mercy, let them rejoice." The repetition serves emphasis and confirmation, and to establish that bounty and mercy alone are the proper objects of rejoicing, to the exclusion of whatever else of the benefits of this world. One of the two verbs is therefore omitted, since the mentioned one indicates it. The *fa'* (the particle "then") enters with the meaning of a conditional (*shart*), as if it were said: "If they rejoice in anything, then let them single out these two for rejoicing." Or: "By the bounty of Allah and His mercy, then let them take care [to seek them], and so let them rejoice in that." The two are the Book of Allah and Islam. In a hadith: "Whoever Allah guides to Islam, and teaches him the Qur'an, and then complains of poverty, Allah will write poverty between his eyes until the day he meets Him," and he recited the verse, **"It is better than what they gather."**

As for the reading *"fa-l-tafrahū"* with the *tā'* (in place of *yā'*), it is the reading of Ibn 'Amir al-Shami (Ibn ʿĀmir al-Shāmī), and Ya'qub (Yaʿqūb) reads it that way as well.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 59:

﴿Say: "Have you considered?"﴾ Tell me. ﴿What Allah has sent down to you of provision﴾: "what" (ma) is in the accusative, governed either by "sent down" (anzala) or by "have you considered" (ara'aitum), meaning: tell me about it. ﴿Then you have made from it lawful and unlawful﴾: you divided it, saying, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," like His saying ﴿What is in the wombs of these cattle is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives﴾ [al-An'am: 139]. Indeed, provisions come forth from the earth, but since their causes were attached to the sky (such as the rain, by which the earth produces plants, and the sun, by which fruits ripen and become luxuriant), their sending down was ascribed to the sky. ﴿Say: "Has Allah permitted you?"﴾ This is connected to "have you considered," and "say" is repeated for emphasis. The meaning is: tell me, "Has Allah permitted you" in making things lawful and unlawful, so that you do this by His permission? ﴿Or do you fabricate against Allah?﴾ Or do you lie against Allah in attributing that to Him? Or the hamza is for denial, and "or" (am) is disjunctive, meaning: "Rather, do you fabricate against Allah?", establishing the fabrication. The verse restrains from being lax regarding the rulings that are asked about, and urges that caution be exercised in them, and that no one should say of anything "permissible" or "not permissible" except after certainty and mastery; otherwise he is a fabricator against the Judge of Judgment (al-Dayyan).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 60:

﴿And what do those think who fabricate lies against Allah, [concerning] the Day of Resurrection?﴾ They attribute that to Him. ﴿On the Day of Resurrection﴾ is in the accusative case (manṣūb) by [the verb of] "thinking" (al-ẓann), and it is a [place] in which the thinking occurs. That is: what did those who fabricate [lies] think would be done to them on that day? It is the Day of Recompense for good and evil deeds, and it is a great threat, since its matter is left vague. ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind﴾ in that He bestowed upon them reason, showed them mercy through revelation, and taught them what is lawful and unlawful. ﴿But most of them do not give thanks﴾ for this blessing, and do not follow what they have been guided to.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 61:

﴿Wa-ma takūnu fī sha'n﴾ "Mā" is negating (mā nāfiyah), and the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ). Sha'n means "matter" (al-amr). ﴿Wa-mā tatlū minhu﴾ "from it" refers to the revelation (al-tanzil), as if it were said: "and you do not recite any Qur'an from the revelation," because every part of it is Qur'an. The pronoun before mention is for magnification of it. Or [the pronoun refers] to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿Wa-lā ta'malūna﴾ "and you do not do," you all together, ﴿min 'amal﴾ "any deed," whatever deed, ﴿illā kunnā 'alaykum shuhūdan﴾ "except that We are witnesses over you," two witnesses, watchful guardians, Who record over you. ﴿Idh tufīḍūna fīh﴾ "when you plunge into it," you engage in it, from afāḍa fī al-amr (to "rush into" a matter) when one surges into it. ﴿Wa-mā ya'zubu 'an Rabbika﴾ "and is not hidden from your Lord," and is not far away and is not absent. With the zāy kasra (ya'izbu), it is 'Alī, meaning "wherever it is." ﴿Min mithqāli dharratin﴾ "of the weight of an atom," the weight of a tiny ant, ﴿fī al-arḍi wa-lā fī al-samā'i wa-lā aṣghara min dhālika wa-lā akbar﴾ "on earth or in heaven, nor anything smaller than that or greater." Ḥamzah read the two (aṣghara and akbar) in the nominative as a mubtada' and khabar. ﴿Illā fī kitābin mubīn﴾ "except that it is in a clear Book," meaning the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfūẓ). Others read the two in the accusative, as negation of the genus (nafy al-jins). Here "the earth" is placed before "the heaven," while in Saba' "the heavens" is placed first, because the conjunction is with waw. Its rule is the rule of the dual (tathniyah).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 62:

﴿Verily, the awliya' (friends/allies) of God﴾ are those who take God as their ally through obedience, and whom God takes as His ally through honour; or they are those whom God has guided by the proof (burhan) that He gave them, so they undertake the upholding of its truth and mercy toward His creation; or they are those who love one another for God's sake, not for ties of kinship between them nor for wealth they exchange; or they are the believers who are God-fearing (muttaqun), by the evidence of the second verse. ﴿No fear shall be upon them﴾ when people fear, ﴿nor shall they grieve﴾ when people grieve.

"Those who believed" (alladhina amanu) is in the accusative by an implied verb, meaning "I mean," or because it is an attributive (sifah) of "friends (awliya')," or it is in the nominative as the predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject (mubtada'), i.e., "they are those who believed." ﴿And they used to be mindful of God﴾: they used to guard against polytheism (al-shirk) and sins (al-ma'asi).

﴿For them is good news in the life of this world﴾. This is what God has given good news of to the believers who are mindful of Him, in more than one place in His Book. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is the good dream that a Muslim sees, or that is seen for him." He (peace be upon him) also said: "Prophethood has departed, but the bearers of good news remain, and the good dream is one part of forty-six parts of prophethood." This is because the period of revelation (wahy) was twenty-three years, and during six months of it he was commanded in sleep to give warning, and six months out of twenty-three years is one part of forty-six parts. Or: it is the people's love for him and good mention of him. Or: ﴿for them is good news﴾ at the moment of death (nazʿ), by their seeing their place in Paradise. ﴿And in the Hereafter﴾ is Paradise. ﴿There is no changing of the words of God﴾: no alteration of His statements and no breaking of His promises. ﴿That﴾ refers to their being given good news in both abodes. ﴿It is the supreme triumph﴾. Both sentences are a parenthetical clause (iʿtirāḍ), and it is not necessary that speech follow a parenthetical clause, as when you say: "So-and-so speaks the truth, and the truth is clear," and then fall silent. (p-31)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 65:

﴿And let not their speech grieve you﴾: their denial, their threats, and their consultation about devising your destruction and nullifying your affair. ﴿Indeed, the might﴾: this is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) with the sense of causation (ta'lil), as if it were said: "Why should I not grieve?" and so it is said: indeed, the might ﴿belongs to Allah﴾ entirely. Indeed, victory and domination are in the dominion of Allah entirely; none possesses any part of them, neither they nor others. So He overcomes them and gives you victory over them. ﴿Allah has decreed: "Surely I and My messengers shall prevail"﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21] ﴿Indeed We surely help Our messengers﴾ [Ghafir: 51]. Or, by it every mighty one gains might: He grants you might, your religion and your family.

The pause (waqf) on "qawluhum" is obligatory, lest "Indeed, the might" become part of the speech of the disbelievers. ﴿Entirely﴾ is a circumstantial accusative (hal). ﴿He is the All-Hearing﴾ of what they say, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of what they plot and resolve upon; and He will requite them for that.

ۗ Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth. He means the rational beings, who are the angels and the two weighty creatures (humans and jinn). He specified them to indicate that if these belong to Him and are in His dominion, and none of them is fit for lordship (rububiyyah) or to be a partner with Him in it, then what is beyond them, of what does not reason, is more worthy that it should not have a equal or partner with Him.

﴿And those who call upon other than Allah as partners do not follow.﴾ Ma (ما) here is negative, meaning: they do not follow the reality of partners, even though they call them partners, because partnership with Allah in lordship is impossible. ﴿They follow only conjecture.﴾ That is, they follow nothing but their own assumption that they are partners of Allah. ﴿And they are only guessing.﴾ That is, they estimate and conjecture, assuming that they are partners, an assumption that is false.

Alternatively, ma is interrogative, meaning: what is it that they follow? According to this reading, "shuraka'" (partners) is in the accusative governed by "yad'un" (they call upon), and according to the first reading it is governed by "yattabi'" (they follow). The original form would have been: "wa-ma yattabi'u alladhina yad'una min dun Allah shuraka' shuraka'," but one of the two was omitted because the meaning is clear. The omitted element is the object of "yad'una," or the relative pronoun is coordinated with "man," as if it were said: "And to Allah belongs what those who call upon other than Allah as partners follow," that is, to Him belong their partners.

Then he drew attention to the greatness of His power and the comprehensiveness of His blessing upon His servants, by His saying ﴿He it is who made the night for you that you may rest therein﴾. That is: He made the night dark for you so that you may rest in it from the fatigue of moving about during the day, ﴿and the day to see by﴾, illuminated so that you may see in it the pursuits of your provision and your gains. ﴿Verily in that are signs for a people who hear﴾, hearing that is reminded and takes heed.

﴿They say: "God has taken a son." Glory be to Him!﴾ This is a declaration of His transcendence (tanzih, His being free of any deficiency) above taking a son, and an expression of wonder at their foolish statement.

﴿He is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani)﴾ This is the reason for negating a son. One who seeks a son is either weak, so that he may be strengthened by him, or poor, so that he may be helped by him, or humbled, so that he may gain honor through him. All of these are signs of need. Whoever is self-sufficient and not in need, a son is negated from him. Also, because a son is a part of the father, this requires that the father be composite, and every composite is contingent (mumkin), and every contingent thing needs another. Therefore it is originated (hadith), and it is impossible for the Eternal (qadim) to have a son.

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth﴾ in ownership, and sonship does not combine with that ownership.

﴿You have no authority for this﴾ meaning: you have no proof for this statement. The preposition "bi" in "bihadha" (for this) should properly be connected to the verb of "inda-kum" (you have). It may also be taken so that the statement itself occupies the place of "sultan" (authority), as in your saying: "ma 'indakum bi-ardikum mawz" (there is no banana in your land). It is as if it were said: "If there is, in what you say, any authority." When He negated proof from them, He made them people without knowledge, so He said: ﴿Do you say about God what you do not know?﴾
